title: Weekly home pool routine and water level
audience: Pool service technicians and maintenance staff who carry out or check a routine visit to a home pool
learningOutcomes: Set out a fixed weekly visit sequence for a home pool and mark each task as done, skipped or referred
Confirm the water level against the minimum height at the skimmer opening and explain why a low level harms the pump
Empty and inspect skimmer and strainer baskets and decide when a basket needs attention before the next visit
Name the tasks a routine visit does not cover and the written instruction needed before they start

instruction.heading: Why a fixed weekly sequence matters
instruction.body: A home pool needs a short visit that repeats the same way each week more than it needs a large occasional effort. The UK handbook behind this lesson describes a weekly routine that takes only a short time when the pool and plant are well designed. The routine works because the same tasks happen in the same order, so a skipped step becomes visible quickly. Choose a set day and record every visit on the same form. Readings and observations then line up across weeks, and a change in water level, debris or filter pressure can be seen rather than remembered. The handbook is a 2011 UK document. Its times, products and temperatures are not Australian facts. What transfers is the sequence and the reason for each step.

instruction.heading: Confirm the water level before anything runs
instruction.body: Read the water level before the pump is started. The pump draws water through the skimmer opening, and when the level falls below the point the skimmer weir needs, the pump begins to draw air. Air in the suction line stops circulation and can harm the pump. Water leaves a pool through splashing, evaporation and backwashing, so in hot weather the level can drop noticeably in a week. Top up only to the level the equipment is designed for and the operator plan allows. If you cannot see the skimmer weir or the level is unclear, avoid running the pump until the level is confirmed. Write the level and any top-up on the record. A large top-up every week can indicate a leak, and that is a referral item rather than a routine task.

instruction.heading: Baskets, strainers and skimming
instruction.body: Empty the skimmer basket plus inspect the pump strainer basket at the frequency the site plan sets. Where trees overhang the pool, leaves and blossom can fill a skimmer basket quickly, so the visit frequency may need to rise in some seasons. The skimmer catches floating debris and the filter traps the fine particles that pass it. A full basket reduces flow. The UK handbook sets a weekly check for the pump strainer, while the manufacturer manual for one pump sets a more frequent interval. Where the two differ, use the more frequent interval unless the operator plan sets another. Before closing a strainer lid, check the lid seal and the O-ring. Torn mesh, cracked lids or a damaged seal go to the owner or operator for replacement.

instruction.heading: The chemistry check and what the visit may change
instruction.body: Test sanitiser and pH using the kit method the owner or operator has agreed. Read the colour in daylight against a white background, compare it with the card in the kit, and record the reading as a value with the time, method and tester. Compare the result with the target in the written plan. The handbook says to check pH and sanitiser before use, even on a pool that is serviced regularly. Make only the adjustments the plan allows for the visit. Cloudy water changes which readings can be trusted, so record the cloudiness and refer it. The disinfection and pH decisions themselves are covered in “Disinfection chemistry and pH interpretation”, and the dosing rules are covered in “Dosing systems and chlorine-gas prevention”.

instruction.heading: Tasks a routine visit does not include
instruction.body: Do not empty a pool to clean it or to lower its level without professional advice. Water pressure from the ground can push a concrete shell upward and can lift or displace a liner. An empty pool is also more dangerous for anyone who falls in, because injuries are more likely than in a full pool. Winterising, equipment repair, electrical work and gas work all sit outside a routine visit. Each of them needs a separate written instruction and, where it applies, the licence described in the licence notices of “Pool chemical handling and storage at home”, “Home pool heating systems: operation and safe limits” and “Home pool troubleshooting and liner repair”. A routine visit records what was checked. It does not show that the water is safe to use.

procedure: Confirm the site, the owner or operator, and the scope of the visit against the work order.
Check and record the water level. Top up only to the height in the plan or the equipment design.
Confirm the pump is on as expected and the suction valves are in their operating positions before you rely on the flow.
Empty and inspect the skimmer basket plus the pump strainer basket. Check the lids and seals before closing.
Clear floating debris from the surface with a net or collector.
Vacuum the floor if the schedule calls for it, using the method in “Vacuuming, vacuum to waste and automated cleaners”.
Run the filter at the agreed time and note the gauge reading.
Test sanitiser and pH, and record both values with time, method and tester.
Record any task you did not complete and the reason, then leave a short note for the owner or operator.

workedExamples.situation: A home pool with a tree hanging over the fence. The water is visibly below the middle of the skimmer opening. The owner asks you to switch the pump on straight away because guests arrive tonight.
workedExamples.reasoning: Avoid running the pump with a low level. Top up to the working level the plan allows, confirm the level is steady, and then start the pump and watch that it draws water rather than air. Record the low level, the top-up if known, and the leaf load in the baskets. Tell the owner that leaves fill baskets faster under trees, and that the trimming of overhanging branches is their decision.

workedExamples.situation: During the chemistry check the water looks cloudy and the test reading falls outside the range in the written plan.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you adjust the chemistry to the plan range and mark the visit complete?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Cloudy water means the reading may not represent the whole pool. Record the reading, the cloudiness and the time, then refer the matter to the operator or owner. Adjust only what the plan allows for this visit, and do not describe the water as safe for bathing.

equipmentAndPpe: Work order and written site plan or operator instruction
Water level reference marks at the skimmer opening, or as set by the operator
Test kit for sanitiser and pH, with colour card and reagents within date
Gloves for handling baskets and strainers
Visit record sheet or job app

commonErrors.error: Starting the pump before the water level is checked
commonErrors.prevention: Check and record the level first. Avoid running the pump until the level is confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Recording a chemistry reading without its time, method or tester
commonErrors.prevention: Write the time, method, reagent batch and tester on every reading.

commonErrors.error: Adjusting chemistry beyond what the written plan allows
commonErrors.prevention: Adjust only what the plan permits. Refer everything else.

commonErrors.error: Treating a clean-looking pool as a safe pool
commonErrors.prevention: A visit records what was checked. Clear water does not prove the water is safe to use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Avoid using the pool should the floor be not visible at every moment. Stop and refer when the water is too cloudy to see the floor.
Do not empty a pool without expert advice. Ground water pressure can damage the structure, and an empty pool increases the injury risk for anyone who falls in.
Do not run a pump while the water level is unconfirmed, because low water can let air into the pump and damage it.
This lesson does not grant a licence or authority for chemical, electrical, gas or heater work.

qualityStandard: Every task on the weekly sequence is recorded as done, skipped or referred.
The water level is recorded before the pump is run, and the pump runs only once the level is confirmed.
Each chemistry reading carries a time, a method and a tester.
Each referral names the owner or operator, the reason and the time.
documentationEvidence: Visit record showing water level, basket condition, filter gauge reading and both chemistry readings
Note of any task not done and the reason
Referral note sent to the owner or operator, with time sent
summary: A fixed sequence with the water level checked first prevents most routine damage.
Chemistry results are useful only with a time, a method and a tester recorded.
Draining, repairs and electrical or gas work are not routine tasks and need written instruction.

knowledgeChecks.question: A home pool's water level sits below the middle of the skimmer opening. What is the correct first action?
options: Confirm the level, then top up to the level the plan allows before the pump runs
Take the skimmer basket out so that the level rises and leave the lid off
Lower the filter pressure to compensate for the low level and keep the pump on
Run the pump to circulate the water and check the level afterwards

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the time and method recorded with each chemistry reading?
options: So the reading can be rounded to the nearest whole number and the owner can see the number on the wall
So a reading can be checked against its method and time, and late or cloudy readings can be identified
So the owner can compare the result with a neighbour's pool and the neighbour's pool can be tested too
It is only needed for insurance and has no technical value and the insurer asks for it each year

knowledgeChecks.question: The water looks cloudy and the test result falls outside the range in the written plan. What should you do?
options: Adjust the chemistry to the usual range and mark the visit complete
Drain a part of the pool to reduce the volume and refill it with fresh water later on
Record the reading, the cloudiness and the time, and refer to the owner or operator
Ask a child in the household whether the water feels safe and if they say yes, carry on
